audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for child kingship, restoration of high places, Baal/Asherah and heavenly-host worship, child-through-fire, divination and spirit-practitioner terminology, temple pluralization, prophetic collective-judgment rhetoric, Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood, Amon's assassination, retaliatory execution of conspirators, and Josiah's succession.

verses.restored: Twelve years old was Manasseh when he became king, and fifty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Hephzibah.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to abominations of nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before children of Israel.
He rebuilt high places Hezekiah his father destroyed, raised altars for Baal, made an Asherah as Ahab king of Israel had done, bowed to all host of heavens, and served them.
He built altars in house of YHWH, concerning which YHWH said, In Jerusalem I will put my name.
He built altars for all host of heavens in two courts of house of YHWH.
He made his son pass through fire, practiced soothsaying and omens, and dealt with a medium and spirit-knowers. He multiplied doing evil in eyes of YHWH, provoking him.

He set carved image of Asherah he had made in house concerning which YHWH said to David and Solomon his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all tribes of Israel, I will put my name for all time.
I will not again make foot of Israel wander from land I gave their fathers, if only they guard to do according to all I commanded them and according to all Torah my servant Moses commanded them.
But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than nations YHWH destroyed from before children of Israel.
YHWH spoke through his servants the prophets, saying,
Because Manasseh king of Judah did these abominations, doing more evil than all Amorites before him, and caused Judah also to sin with his idols,
therefore thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: Look, I am bringing evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, such that both ears of everyone hearing it shall tingle.
I will stretch over Jerusalem measuring line of Samaria and plummet of house of Ahab. I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping and turning it upon its face.
I will abandon remnant of my inheritance and give them into hand of their enemies; they shall become prey and plunder to all their enemies,
because they did evil in my eyes and provoked me from day their fathers came out of Egypt even to this day.
Moreover Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth, besides his sin by which he caused Judah to sin, doing evil in eyes of YHWH.
Remaining acts of Manasseh, all he did, and his sin that he sinned, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
Manasseh lay with his fathers and was buried in garden of his house, in garden of Uzza. Amon his son became king in his place.
Twenty-two years old was Amon when he became king, and two years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, as Manasseh his father had done.
He walked in all way his father walked, served idols his father served, and bowed to them.
He abandoned YHWH, Divine of his fathers, and did not walk in way of YHWH.
Servants of Amon conspired against him and put king to death in his house.
People of land struck all who conspired against king Amon, and people of land made Josiah his son king in his place.
Remaining acts of Amon that he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
They buried him in his grave in garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son became king in his place.

translation_notes: Manasseh begins ruling at twelve. A child king remains vulnerable to court systems, inherited institutions, and adult advisers; youth does not remove later accountability or prove children should wield sovereign power.
Making his son pass through fire is child abuse or sacrifice. No parental, royal, or religious authority can make a child's body an offering.
Medium and spirit-knower vocabulary describes ancient religious specialists. The text may not support witch-hunts, occult panic, misogyny, or violence toward contemporary spiritual practitioners.
The narrator condemns Manasseh's placement of other sacred practices in the temple. This covenantal polemic may not authorize attacks on other religions or forced religious uniformity.
The wiping-dish image and abandonment of the remnant express collective destruction. Such rhetoric is morally dangerous and may not justify punishing a population for a ruler's acts.
Verse 16 identifies Manasseh's abundant shedding of innocent blood as central to his reign. The victims remain unnamed but must not disappear behind disputes about ritual.
The claim that Manasseh exceeded the Amorites is ancient ethnic polemic and cannot become contempt toward modern peoples or justification of conquest.
Amon is assassinated by palace servants, and the people then execute the conspirators. Neither murder nor retaliatory killing supplies due process.
The mothers Hephzibah and Meshullemeth are named as lineage markers, not causes of their sons' actions.
Chronicles preserves a substantially different Manasseh tradition including captivity, repentance, and reform; the witnesses require separate treatment rather than forced harmonization.
safety_note: Do not normalize child sacrifice, persecute spiritual practitioners or minority religions, blame an entire population for a king's crimes, erase Manasseh's victims, glorify assassination, or celebrate retaliatory execution. Center children, innocent blood, institutional accountability, and the limits of dynastic and prophetic punishment theology.
